verdictProvider: No subagent judged anything in this round; the tester's own session ran every check, so no provider or model needs naming.

fingerprint.result: changed, so this was a full round
fingerprint.why: The merge brought in main's block index (#2210), which leases a ninth maintenance loop (block-index). This branch's repair makes ten, so leasePoolSize goes from 9 to 10, and the README's loop count and main.go's goroutine order were resolved to match. Retro's commits (docs/solutions and the removal of .legion/) are outside the fingerprint.

implementerProof.how: Drove the merged head independently on dispatch:local: two processes sharing the leases, closes through the daemon's new SetStatus that parses the response, block ids and references across a close, races, an upgrade from main b69f636f, the unloadable close and rebuild, the round-9 web-app probes, and the browser suites.

proof.criterion: Every leased maintenance loop, the asks repair and main's new block index included, runs once across processes with leasePoolSize 10
proof.surface: Two head processes (A on 8797, B on 8796) on one Postgres database for 13 minutes
proof.command: run-server.sh twice on tester_r13; drive closes and races through both; then grep the 'leased pass ran|skipped' lines from both logs
proof.observed: B ran issue-ask-repair once at 06:55:35 and A skipped it at 06:55:36. block-index ran 26 times on B and A skipped it 25 times. suggestion-outcomes, architecture-import, delivery-reconcile and reference-excerpts each ran on B with A's skips matching. No pass ran on both.
proof.negativeControl: Each A skip line is the lease refusing a second holder; with a pool short of the leased names a loop would wait for a connection instead of logging a ran or skipped line, and every loop logged one.

proof.criterion: Close by a person, an agent session and the Legion daemon withdraws every open ask naming the closer and changes nothing else; the daemon's SetStatus, which now parses the PATCH response, reads a last_seq equal to the issue's; reopen restores the asks; block ids and block references survive the close
proof.surface: dispatch:local with the branch's CLI and the daemon's dispatch.HTTPClient.SetStatus (rebuilt for main's new signature)
proof.command: seed.ts TT 3; dcli doc-read --issue TT-1 --blocks; alice cookie PATCH TT-1; dcli issue-update --issue TT-2 --status done; daemonclose TT-3 done and GET TT-3; state.ts; --blocks again; reopen TT-1 (PATCH response and GET); --blocks again; comment citing dispatch://TT-1/spec#b-563e44c0-…; daemonclose TT-1; dcli read --ref of that block
proof.observed: SetStatus answered status=done last_seq=26, and GET answered last_seq=26. On each issue open_asks is 0 and the approval draft; d1, p1, p3, h1 and ap read withdrawn by alice | tester-agent-9 | legion-daemon:TT; d2 answered, p2 retracted, p4 resolved; blocks and the copy read resolved; the named versions read d1=open. The --blocks listing differs across the close only in d1's state attribute, and is identical after the reopen. The reopen's response last_seq 32 equals GET's, and the 5 asks are restored. After the close the block reference still resolves, listing the comment under 'Referenced by'.
proof.negativeControl: The same closes on main's build b69f636f left open_asks 5, the approval awaiting and every block open

proof.criterion: Asks already open on closed issues are repaired, naming each closer; later passes write nothing; concurrent and cross-process closes stay consistent; a close beside an unloadable document succeeds and a rebuild shows the withdrawn block resolved
proof.surface: Main's build b69f636f, then the head on the same database; two head processes; dispatch:local
proof.command: Main seeds UP-1..3, adds an unindexed block to each and closes them (alice, old-agent-5, SetStatus); the head boots; two repair passes with an md5 before and after; race.ts resolve 8, double 5, unsettled 6, flip 5; race2.ts 8; UP-4 with notes.md corrupted, daemonclose, rebuild as alice, reopen
proof.observed: Boot: withdrawn=15 restored=0 swept=3, naming alice, old-agent-5 and legion-daemon:UP; the passes left the md5 unchanged. Races: 0 problems on one process and across two. UP-4: close 200 with the ask withdrawn; rebuild 200 with block state="resolved"; after the reopen state="open".
proof.negativeControl: On main's build the three closed issues kept 5 open asks each, the approval awaiting and the blocks open

proof.criterion: The web app after main's editor changes: no false unsent-edit notice in any tested order, and typed text kept exactly once
proof.surface: Dispatch's Playwright harness (chromium and iphone) with a throwaway spec keeping the server's frame order and delaying only Auth where a probe needs it (deleted after); Dispatch's own browser suites
proof.command: Probes 1, 2, 5 and 8 of round 9, --repeat-each 2; bunx playwright test close-withdraws-asks offline-edits doc margin ask-blocks references --project chromium --project iphone
proof.observed: 16 of 16: a closed document stores 0 rows; the reopen then offline then a second close shows no notice; the review's path stores 0 rows with status 'connected'; held stamps, then a cut, typing and a reload give typed 1, '## Held heading' 1, 'held two' 1, '## Detail' 1 and 'second step' 1. Suites: 165 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped.
proof.negativeControl: Round 9: the web apps without the fix (83649d6a's and 52159aaf's connection.ts and pending-sync.ts) failed the review's path 2 of 2 each with 'can't be sent: this document is read-only.'
